annotations.title: Ask the monograph: tax residence, tax jurisdiction, taxpayer status

description: Answers general questions about tax residence and the theory behind it from the monograph by DoubleTaxation's legal expert, Yevhen Marynchak, "The Financial and Legal Nexus between an Individual and a State: Tax Residence, Citizenship and Tax Jurisdiction in a Modern World" (3rd edition, revised and expanded, 2026, in English; law as of November 2026): 777 passages of the book's own text covering economic theories of taxation (Smith, Schanz, Wicksell–Lindahl) and concepts of legal understanding; tax sovereignty and tax jurisdiction (interstate, state, local, offshore), the genuine-link requirement (Nottebohm, Commission v. Malta); the tax legal status, legal personality and rights of an individual taxpayer; citizenship-based taxation and citizenship by investment; the genesis of the residence principle (19th century, League of Nations, OECD Model Article 4) and its criteria and tie-breaker; source taxation; modern trends; residence in war and mass displacement; remote work and digital nomads; automatic exchange of information (CRS); ultra-high-net-worth individuals; the UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation; the author's model of the financial and legal nexus and the algorithmic determination of residence; a comparative table of residence criteria. Each passage comes with the book's section, printed page and a link to find it on Google Books. Use "query" in English key words (translate if needed); call without arguments for an overview and the table of contents. Not for a person's own status: use check_residency.

ids.description: Return these entries by id (from an earlier result).

kind.description: Limit to one kind of passage (e.g. definition, history, proposal, conclusion).

query.description: The user's question or its key words, in English (translate if needed), e.g. "why did citizenship stop determining tax duties", "digital nomads residence" or "displaced persons centre of vital interests".

section.description: Limit to one part of the book: a chapter number ("5") includes its subsections and conclusions ("5.2", "5.C"); alone, lists that part's passages in order.

topic.description: Short overview of one theme instead of a search: what_is = What tax residence is; origin = Where the concept comes from; why_it_matters = Why tax residence matters; criteria = How tax residence is determined; citizenship = Tax residence and citizenship; tax_jurisdiction = Tax sovereignty and tax jurisdiction; modern_challenges = Residence today: mobility, war, transparency, the very wealthy; future = The future: algorithmic determination of residence.
